# $crav1-host-setup

lane: cross-cutting | group: Commit and pull request | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.115.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Change one Azure DevOps or GitHub setting that does not live in the repo, through a checked-in script applied after a yes and read back live.
use_when: You need a branch policy, required build, reviewers, an approval or a variable group set on the host
reads: Reads the ask, `docs/system/repos.md`, the git remote, the repo's pipeline YAML and, when signed in, the live host setting (`az` or `gh`).
writes: After an explicit yes to the shown script, applies the setting on the host, runs the read-back, and commits the script (`infra/ado/<name>.sh` or `infra/github/<name>.sh`) on a work branch.
leaves alone: Leaves secret values, specs, plans, pull requests and threads alone. Does not push.
limits: Not signed in, or a headless run, drafts and stops without applying. Something the host reads from the repo is code and is routed to its lane. A larger ask is offered as a spec.
flow:
- the apply confirm is one card.
- `yes (Recommended)` runs the script as shown.
- Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer and redraft the script.
- You describe it; the kit drafts a checked-in `az` or `gh` script under `infra/ado/` or `infra/github/` with a what and why comment above each command, and generates the manual steps from those comments.
- `yes (Recommended)` runs them.
- A typed change on that card's free-text answer redrafts them until yes.
- It runs the script, reads the live setting back with the script's `check` part and commits the script on a work branch.
- Done means the read-back says `ok`.
- Service connections and secret values are always manual: the script only checks they exist by name.
- The plan route (plan-from-spec, build-tasks, verify) uses the same shared reference for `(host setup)` tasks, so both routes write the same script.
called_by: Called by the user. Plan tasks marked `(host setup)` follow its shared reference inside build-tasks.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: $crav1-open-pr; $crav1-pr-status
first: `$crav1-host-setup Require a green build of <pipeline> on <branch> in <repo>.`
walkthrough: from-host-setup.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.207.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-host-setup.md
